prediction:
THOUGHT: Rapid onset (symptoms began 1 day after starting ulixertinib and presented on day 10), bilateral involvement, mild visual acuity reduction, widespread acneiform dermatitis, and the fundus/OCT findings (multifocal, small yellow subretinal deposits that are hyperautofluorescent; OCT showing multiloculated/coalesced subretinal fluid, subretinal debris located between the RPE and the interdigitation zone, plus some CME) strongly point to a drug-induced serous retinopathy from MAPK-pathway inhibition. Ulixertinib is an ERK inhibitor (downstream of BRAF/MEK) and ERK/MEK inhibitors are well-known to cause a characteristic, typically bilateral, multifocal serous retinopathy (so-called MEK-inhibitor–associated retinopathy or ERK-inhibitor–associated retinopathy) that is often reversible and associated with acneiform rash. Alternative diagnoses to consider (but less likely given the timing, bilateral multifocal pattern, and classic imaging) include central serous chorioretinopathy, inflammatory causes such as Vogt–Koyanagi–Harada, paraneoplastic or immune-related retinopathy related to cancer or prior immunotherapy, and multifocal exudative detachments from choroidal metastases.

DIAGNOSIS:
1. ERK/MEK inhibitor–associated multifocal serous retinopathy (ulixertinib-associated retinopathy) — most likely given immediate temporal relationship to ulixertinib, bilateral multifocal SRF with subretinal debris and hyperautofluorescent yellow deposits, and accompanying acneiform rash.
2. Central serous chorioretinopathy (multifocal/atypical) — can produce serous detachments and subretinal material but less consistent with the rapid drug-related onset and diffuse bilateral multifocal pattern.
3. Vogt–Koyanagi–Harada–spectrum posterior uveitis (atypical presentation) — bilateral SRF and subretinal material can occur but would more commonly have anterior chamber/vitreous inflammation and systemic prodrome, which are absent.
4. Paraneoplastic or immune-related retinopathy (cancer-associated retinopathy/autoimmune retinopathy or immune checkpoint inhibitor–related ocular toxicity) — possible given history of cancer and prior pembrolizumab, but the OCT/fundus pattern and temporal link to ulixertinib favor a drug toxicity rather than classic paraneoplastic retinal degeneration.
5. Bilateral choroidal metastases with exudative (serous) retinal detachment — lung adenocarcinoma can metastasize to the choroid and cause serous detachments, but metastatic lesions usually produce focal mass lesions and are less likely to present as numerous small hyperautofluorescent subretinal deposits and rapid symmetric onset after a new systemic agent.

Case Information:
A 64-year-old woman presented to the emergency department with bilateral progressive blurred vision. Medical history includes lung adenocarcinoma managed with partial lobectomy 4 years prior, with local recurrence treated with 6 cycles of carboplatin, pemetrexed, and pembrolizumab. A second recurrence was detected during pembrolizumab monotherapy. She began receiving 600 mg of ulixertinib twice daily. Symptoms started 1 day after starting ulixertinib, presenting to clinic on day 10 of treatment.

Physical Examination:
Visual acuity of 20/40 OU with pinhole improvement of 20/25 OU. External examination showed diffuse acneiform dermatitis involving 80% of body surface area from head to toe. Anterior segment examination unremarkable. Fundus examinations of both eyes demonstrated multifocal, yellow, subretinal deposits in the posterior pole that were hyperautofluorescent on fundus autofluorescence.

Diagnostic Tests:
- Imaging Studies:    1. Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT):       Image Description: Shows cystoid macular edema (CME), coalesced subretinal fluid (SRF), and subretinal debris inferiorly between the retinal pigment epithelium and the interdigitation zone        2. Optos Fundus Photography:       Image Description: Yellow, circular globules in the posterior pole that were hyperautofluorescent on fundus autofluorescence, with conglomeration around the arcades        3. Genetic Testing:       Result: Positive for BRAF mutation
